utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- you may sit down. Please sit down. It's five past 6.00, and we will finish at 7.00. The Prosecution may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness BA, you were telling us before the break about the billeting of your unit in places where there were Muslim inhabitants and you receiving better support as members of that brigade than other units did. I'm just saying that to direct you to where we were a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Armies have different units, such as reconnaissance brigades, assault brigades, logistics brigades or units, intelligence units, and so on. What sort of unit was the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: Up until 1994, the brigade had the same duties as all other battalions in any other brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When units go into combat in a coordinated plan where you've got different units from different brigades or battalions operating in the same combat operation, some go in -- some units go first, other units go second; other units come from the sides. Where did your unit go -- where did your unit feature in the order of attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: On the whole, it escorted the reconnaissance and sabotage platoon. It would accompany them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The reconnaissance and the sabotage platoon, was it the first one to go in to battle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: In most of the operations, yes, that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What sort of support did your battalion -- sorry, your -- your battalion provide to the reconnaissance and sabotage platoon when it went into battle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: It mainly provided military support, if there were certain obstacles, if the platoon encountered strong resistance, then it would provide fire support, if the reconnaissance and sabotage platoon encountered such resistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What you've just said indicated coordination between the reconnaissance and sabotage platoon and your own unit. Who coordinated or issued the orders for your unit and the reconnaissance and sabotage platoon to operate together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: It was mostly through company commanders and commanders of the reconnaissance and sabotage platoons. They would coordinate -- they would be involved in such coordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Military units typically have battle cries when they go into combat. What was your brigade's battle cry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: The only battle cry used by members of the 7th Muslim Brigade was Tekbir-U-Alah.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you -- how did you use Tekbir-U-Alah? Can you explain that to the Trial Chamber, and who you used it at.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: All the members used it, on the whole. It was an expression which provided members of the 7th Muslim Brigade with more confidence and it also spread fear. We had the impression that it spread fear among the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you used it to spread fear and to give the brigade more confidence. At what volume did the members call out "Tekbir-U-Alah"? I mean, how loudly did you call it out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: Well, each individual would cry out "Allah-u-ekber" of his own accord and as loudly as he could. And if you have 100 or 200 members who cry this out, then it creates a substantial noise.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The members of the reconnaissance and sabotage platoon, were they also -- were they attached to the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade or were they attached to other units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand the beginning of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. You referred to escorting a reconnaissance and sabotage platoon. Was this platoon part of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade or attached to another brigade or unit of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: As far as I know, they worked within the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did they likewise call out that battle cry or was it confined to members of your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, they used that battle cry too.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to ask you now about the Mujahedin in Zenica and Central Bosnia in 1992 and 1993. What can you tell the Trial Chamber about the arrival in Central Bosnia of Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: Small groups arrived, groups of two or three men on the whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did they arrive from and where did they go to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: From various countries, not just from one country. They would pass through on the whole and find accommodation in their centres. Some didn't even pass through the brigade. They would go to where their men were already located.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll come back to that answer in a moment. When did you notice the arrival -- first notice the arrival of these Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: Perhaps in October or November 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The answer before was "Some didn't even pass through the brigade. They would go to where their men were already located." Where were their men already located? That's the ones who didn't pass through the brigade.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to tell the Trial Chamber about those who did pass through your brigade, as you said a moment ago. How many became members of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: I don't know whether you could say that they became members of the brigade. They were never part of the brigade's operations. At the beginning, some of them would stay in the brigade for a day or two, sleep over there. They would be provided with some sort of accommodation, until they moved on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What can you tell the Trial Chamber about training camps that the Mujahedin had in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: In the beginning, when the Muslim Brigade was being formed, as far as I can remember there was a place where foreigners would provide men with training, would train men.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which place was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: It was in Arnauti, a camp in Arnauti.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And who were the men that were providing this training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there were three or four Turks.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And who were these Turks training? Which men were they training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: They were training the men who had volunteered for this training.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know of any members of your brigade receiving training from those three or four Turks at Arnauti?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did -- how many men from your brigade that you know of went for training with these Turks at Arnauti?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: That training was given at the beginning, when the 7th Muslim Brigade was formed, at a time when it still didn't bear that name and I took part in the training too.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many other men from your brigade were there, apart from you, receiving this training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: In the group I was in, there were about another 20 members.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please tell the Trial Chamber about the training. What happened at the training camp? What sort of training was provided? How long was it for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: It lasted about ten days. It mostly had to do with preparations, physical stamina, and getting to know the weapons. So it was a period in October 1992, and the brigade hadn't been formed yet. People didn't know what equipment was, what weapons were, and what it meant to go into the field and to war, so this involved training for fitness, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who ordered you to undertake the training with these Turks at Arnauti?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness has already said that the men volunteered, so this question has already been answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I withdraw it and I'll rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you come to be aware that there was the option or possibility of volunteering for training with the Turks in Arnauti?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. That was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to ask you about other training camps run by the Mujahedin. What other camps were you aware of that the Mujahedin was running, for training or whatever other purpose, in Central Bosnia in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: The only camp that existed at the time, I never saw it. I heard about it. It was in Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of the Mujahedin training camps at Mehurici and Arnauti, based upon your experience of having gone there for training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: I can only speak about the camp in Arnauti. I can't say anything about the other camp in Mehurici, as I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please confine yourself to Arnauti, then. My question is: What was the purpose of the Mujahedin training camp at Arnauti, based upon your experience of having trained there?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object again. The witness has answered this question in detail of the Mujahedin training camp at Arnauti, based upon your experience of having trained there?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object again. The witness has answered this question in detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I can certainly rephrase it, to expand it beyond just training.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Apart from training, Witness BA, was there any purpose that you learned of for the Mujahedin having a training camp at Arnauti, based upon your experience of having been there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you aware of members of your brigade going for training with the Mujahedin at the Mehurici camp?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I want to object. The witness has already stated that he knows nothing about this area. He said that he only knew about the camp in Arnauti.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's not quite correct. The witness said he was aware of one at Mehurici. My question is whether he is aware of any of his brigade members going for training there. They're two different issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Witness, could you answer the question. Apparently there was a second camp in Mehurici, and the question was: Were there any members of the 7th Brigade who were trained in that camp, as far as you know? If you don't know -- as far as you know, were any of your comrades or other soldiers trained in this camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to ask you about whether Mujahedin joined the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade before January 1993. Were there any Mujahedin members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade or working within the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade before January 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: The only operation in which the Mujahedin participated was in Visegrad in 1992, on the 27th of December, 1992. That's the only one in which they participated with members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you say "participated," do you mean as members of the brigade or working in coordination with the brigade, in the combat operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: I wouldn't know how to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you present in that combat -- sorry, did you participate in that combat operation yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What role did the Mujahedin have in that operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was to die.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you see them do in that operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: In one of the operations in which 4 or 5 kilometres of the line was attacked, you couldn't see what was happening, so I didn't see what they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said as far as you could remember, their role was to die. What did you mean by "it was to die"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: I said this because as far as I remember, 20 or more Mujahedin got killed in that operation, if that information is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were there -- did members of your brigade die as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were relations like between your brigade and those Mujahedin after that particular operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: That is, I think, when we broke all links with the Mujahedins.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you break links with the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: That is a question that I cannot answer properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you aware of any disputes between the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade and the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: There was a dispute during -- in fact, after that operation between them and the command in Visoko and the command of our brigade. There were officers of our brigade who were abused by the Mujahedin during that dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your information about the supplies -- or the source of the supplies that the Mujahedin had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: I could not answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were there Mujahedin members of the 2nd Battalion up until January 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I turn now to the topic of Dusina, Witness BA. It is an agreed fact in this trial between the Defence and the Prosecution that there was an attack in the vicinity of Dusina on about the 25th of January, 1993, in which the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade participated. Did your battalion participate in the attack on Dusina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Prosecutor referred to some agreed fact between the Prosecution and the Defence. We never agreed as regards the attack. All we agreed to was that a certain number of people got killed during the fighting in Dusina, and I would like the Prosecutor to confirm this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel for the Prosecution, the Defence does not acknowledge that there is agreement between you regarding what you quoted. She confirms that there was fighting in that area at that time, but there is no agreement as to an attack, so the Defence does not agree with the argument that members of the 7th Brigade were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- Your Honours, the Defence is not surprised that the Prosecution now wishes to avail itself of agreed facts, because they are designed to speed up the proceedings. But what the Prosecution would be well advised to do is to quote the relevant section from our agreed facts. The subject indeed falls within the scope of agreed facts but not exactly in the way that was referred to by the Prosecution. I would, therefore, ask my learned friend for a quotation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just -- I mean, I didn't quote from the agreed facts. I paraphrased to try and speed things up and get to the point because I thought there was no dispute about the fact that this witness was a member of the brigade; the 2nd Battalion participated in the attack on Dusina; that occurred. And I'm referring to, on -- it's page 6503 of the filing -- the joint filing of the 3rd of December, 2003, paragraph 16 and 17 on -- the page numbering is a little bit out. The page says "2" at the bottom. Do Your Honours have page 6503 in front of you or can it be provided to you? I mean, if there is some dispute or the Defence is going back on it, it can, of course, be revisited, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber notes that in paragraph 16 of this agreement it states: "On the 26th of January, 1993, the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade and inter alia the 1st Company of the 2nd Battalion took part in combat operations until 6.00 a.m. This went on in Merdani, Dusina and another village." Does the Defence now dispute the contents of this item?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we don't. In the English text, it says precisely "engaged in combat." But the Prosecutor seems to be saying that we agreed that there was an attack and that we -- what we do know, what we agreed to, is that there was a conflict, but not an attack on Dusina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If I understood this correctly, the disagreement is on the following: The Defence acknowledge that forces were engaged in the relevant area and the Prosecution claim it was an attack; is that so? Yes. Well, if the document were in French, I believe that there would be less disagreement about the language, because it would be clearer. In any case, the Trial Chamber notes that the Defence acknowledges there was fighting but not more than that. I'm now giving the floor to the Prosecution, who may continue with their examination, taking into account this objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness BA, I want to ask you about the combat operations in the Dusina area on the 25th and 26th of January, 1993. Did you, your unit, the 2nd Battalion, participate in combat operations in Dusina on the 25th and 26th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was your battalion divided into companies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: At the time, the battalion was not yet complete, so a smaller part of the battalion took part.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could it be described as a company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: It could.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many members took part?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: Maybe 60 to 80.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your company known as? Did it have a name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: I want had this symbolic name, Musical Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were you ordered to go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: To the confluence of Bosna and Lasva Rivers. Our task was to secure the bridge, to guard the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: I wouldn't know exactly why.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who ordered your company there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I was only a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was your battalion commander on the 25th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the name, if it was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said "I think." Can you please repeat that part of your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: I think Taran or Taran was still the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You were ordered to go to the confluence of the Bosna and Lasva Rivers. Did you in fact go there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you do once you got there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: Most of the time we were guarding that site. There was a loop on the road with forks off to Kakanj and Zenica. Our task was to guard that bridge and that loop.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were you based?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: Right there, in a house nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You just told us about your company. What about other companies or units of the ABiH? Were there other ones there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: I don't know whether any other participants were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you aware of other units in the ABiH having been there immediately before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When did you get to the confluence of the Lasva and Bosna Rivers and how long did you remain there for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: I think two or three days maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The question was when? Can you tell us the date, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was it in relation to the 26th of January, 1993, which is the date the parties have agreed was when the combat operations in Dusina occurred.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: Maybe on the 24th.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did your company go from that point of the confluence of the rivers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: To the Dusina village.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you get to the Dusina village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: Taking a round-about way, across a hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to show you a map, Witness BA, of which I have seven copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everybody will receive a copy of this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, Witness BA, I want you to get the large black texter, which the usher, Mr. Usher, will give you. And please draw a circle around the point which was the confluence of the Lasva and Bosna Rivers where your company went to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please now draw an arrow, like a military-type arrow, and show where you went from there, the direction you took to reach the village of Dusina. Do you know what I mean by a "large military-type arrow," on maps where you see an arrow coming down with a big point on the bottom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just trace your route in arrow sort of formation, dot, dot, sort of line, line, line, arrow, arrow, arrow.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just put an arrow in the direction you were travelling, some arrows on these lines, in the direction in which you were travelling.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which part of Dusina did you go to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: The Muslim part of Dusina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When did you arrive there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: By night.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which side of midnight was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you go to in the Muslim part of Dusina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: The soldiers took up positions inside the village. Some were quartered in houses, some up -- some took up guard duty immediately, and some --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness be asked to repeat the end of the sentence and speak up a little, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness BA, could you please repeat the last part of your question -- sorry, your answer. You said "some were quartered in houses. Some took up guard duty immediately, and some --" it sort of petered out there. And the interpreters are asking you to please speak a little more loudly so they can clearly hear you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: Some were billeted in Mejtef.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: M-e-j-t-e-f.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that another way of saying the Muslim part of Dusina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where is or what is Mejtef?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: The Mejtef was located in the upper part of the village, and "Mejtef" is a temple, a place where prayers take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many soldiers accompanied you to the Muslim part of Dusina and the Mejtef on that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: So in this place of worship, in the Mejtef, there were about 20 of us. I don't know how many more were deployed around the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were there any other soldiers -- sorry, were there any soldiers from other units deployed in Mejtef or the Muslim part of Dusina, apart from those in your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: No, not as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you remain overnight in Dusina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what happened the next morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA
utterances.text: The next morning we received some sort of an assignment to take up positions, be deployed around the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does Your Honour wish me to stop at this point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It is two to 7.00, so we had better adjourn. At this stage would you like to tender the map or would you like to do it tomorrow? Unless you have other questions to ask about the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Would it be marked for identification tonight and I'll tender it in the morning when I've had the witness -- sorry, tomorrow, when I've had the witness put further markings on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please give it a number for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours , the number will be P12, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So it will be P12 marked for identification. It is one to 7.00 now, and we shall resume tomorrow in the afternoon, as envisaged. We shall also sit on Tuesday and Wednesday but not on Thursday or Friday because the Plenary is taking place on those two days, and we shall resume again the following week from Monday to Friday. Witness, since not even the examination-in-chief is completed, please come back tomorrow. We will begin at 2.15, but you should be here earlier. In the meantime, I advise you not to meet or discuss your evidence with either party. So we shall meet again tomorrow and work from 2.15. Have you understood me well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 9th day of December, 2003 at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
